newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bids at $64 passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bids at $64 passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Thursday were bid $64.00 per cwt, steady with this week's active sales, but passed by owners looking for $65.00, feedlot sources said.
"It seems like we're going to get $65.00 next week, so there are some people who still have cattle to sell who are reluctant to take a $64.00 bid," a Panhandle cattleman said.

Fed cattle prices this week were up $2.00 from last week's top amid spillover strength from Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures and higher trending boxed beef cut-out values, several cattle feeders said.

Fed cattle prices also were supported by strong demand from packers reportedly short on live supplies as suggested by pick-up early Thursday of cattle sold on Tuesday at several feedlots, the cattle feeders said.
Demand for cattle also was stoked by a need to have ready inventories on hand to fill beef orders booked earlier in the month, market sources said.
Outlooks for slightly smaller supplies of market-ready cattle in the coming weeks also buoyed cattle prices, the feedlot sources said.
